# Contributing to Growers Network QA Suite

Thank you for contributing to this Playwright regression suite. This guide covers the rules, workflow, and conventions all contributors must follow.

---

## Code of Conduct

- Be respectful in code reviews and comments
- Prefer clarity over cleverness — QA code is read more than it is written
- If you disagree with a convention, open a discussion rather than silently breaking it

---

## Prerequisites

| Tool | Minimum version |
|------|----------------|
| Node.js | 18 LTS |
| npm | 9+ |
| Git | 2.38+ |

Install Playwright browsers after `npm install`:

```bash
npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
```

---

## Getting Started

```bash
# 1. Clone and install
git clone <repo-url>
cd growers_network_QA_Agentic_Solution
npm install
npx playwright install --with-deps chromium

# 2. Verify setup (runs smoke tests)
npm run test:smoke

# 3. Run all tests
npm test
```

---

## Architecture Rules (Non-negotiable)

### Page Object Model

Every page or feature must have a page object class in `src/pages/`:
- Classes extend `BasePage` from `src/pages/base.page.ts`
- Locators are `readonly Locator` properties declared in the constructor
- Methods represent **user actions** — they do not assert or return pass/fail
- `expect()` is never called inside page objects

```typescript
// CORRECT: page object returns a value for the test to assert
async getMainHeading(): Promise<string> {
  return (await this.page.locator('h1').first().textContent()) ?? '';
}

// WRONG: assertion inside a page object method
async verifyHeadingVisible(): Promise<void> {
  await expect(this.page.locator('h1')).toBeVisible(); // NOT allowed here
}
```

### Test files

- Import `test` and `expect` from `@fixtures/site.fixture`, not from `@playwright/test`
- Every `test()` call includes a tag: `@smoke`, `@navigation`, `@forms`, `@functional`, `@visual`, or `@responsive`
- No hardcoded URLs — derive from `siteConfig.url`
- No `page.waitForTimeout()` over 500ms — use Playwright auto-waiting

### TypeScript

- Strict mode is enabled — no `any` without a comment explaining why
- Run `npm run typecheck` before pushing any branch

---

## Test Categories

| Folder | Tag | What it covers |
|--------|-----|----------------|
| `tests/smoke/` | `@smoke` | Site loads, HTTP 200, no console errors |
| `tests/navigation/` | `@navigation` | Nav links, mobile menu, routing |
| `tests/forms/` | `@forms` | Form fields, validation (no submission) |
| `tests/functional/` | `@functional` | Business features, content sections |
| `tests/visual/` | `@visual` | Screenshot regression |
| `tests/responsive/` | `@responsive` | Layout at mobile/tablet/desktop |
| `tests/custom/` | `@custom` | Site-specific, generated by agents |

---

## Form Testing Policy

**Never submit a form.** This protects the site owner from unwanted contact submissions or data pollution.

- You MAY interact with form fields (type, tab, clear)
- You MAY click Submit to trigger browser-side HTML5 validation (which fires before the HTTP request)
- You MUST intercept and cancel the request if browser validation passes
- You MUST NOT assert that a confirmation message appeared after a real submission

---

## Submitting Changes

### Branch naming

```
feat/short-description
fix/what-was-broken
chore/what-was-updated
test/what-was-tested
```

### Before opening a PR

```bash
npm run typecheck       # TypeScript must compile cleanly
npm run lint            # No ESLint errors
npm run test:smoke      # Smoke tests must pass
```

### PR description

Use the PR template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`). Every PR must include:
- What changed and why
- Test tag(s) affected
- Whether visual baselines were updated (if so, attach screenshots)

---

## Visual Regression Baselines

Visual snapshots live in `__snapshots__/`. They are committed to source control.

To update baselines after an intentional UI change:

```bash
npm run baseline
```

Review every changed image before committing. Do not update baselines to silence a failing test without understanding why it changed.

---

## Claude Code Integration

This repo is set up for AI-assisted testing with Claude Code. Available slash commands:

| Command | What it does |
|---------|-------------|
| `/analyze-site` | Inspect live site and update `site.config.json` |
| `/generate-full-suite` | Generate full POM + test suite from scratch |
| `/run-smoke` | Run smoke tests and report results |
| `/update-baseline` | Refresh visual regression baselines |
| `/generate-report` | Generate markdown test report from results |

See `Skills.md` in the repo root for full documentation.

Open an issue tagged `question` or check `README.md` for setup help.
